notes:
Summary:
- Mid-market SaaS (customer success/product) building AI-first in-app chat + KB search.
- Starting on Hosted API to get velocity, evaluating Dedicated if unit economics and latency predictable.

POC / Requirements (from calls):
- Workload: conversational support agent + doc search fallback + reranking for suggested articles.
- Latency targets: p50 < 120ms, p95 < 300ms for chat flows.
- Throughput: steady-state ~ 80–150 QPS during business hours; spiky bursts up to 400 QPS.
- Cost sensitivity: target blended cost <= $0.06 per 1k tokens (cto: "can't accept > $0.08/1k").
- Model preferences: open-model preference but willing to test Redwood-verified variants; want quantization recommendations.
- Routing/fallback needs: geo routing (NA primary, EU read-only), fallback to smaller model for low-cost tier.
- Data controls: VPC for Dedicated, KMS for key management, 13-month retention for logs, audit logging mandatory.

Cost Optimization Workshop (2026-03-05) — key notes:
- SE ran live microbenchmarks comparing floating vs 4-bit and 8-bit quantized variants on representative prompts.
- Results: 4-bit q-profile reduced token compute cost by ~32–45% on top intents with negligible drop in top-1 intent accuracy; 8-bit safe but less savings.
- Batching: suggested variable batch-size strategy; recommend adaptive batching with latency SLO gating — expected 12–20% cost saving at peak, but tail latency needs throttling.
- KV / prefix caching: KB-heavy sessions showed 18% token savings when using prefix+KV cache for repeated doc lookups.
- Unit economics model: Redwood SE shared a draft calc showing Dedicated reserved capacity breaks even vs Hosted at ~900M tokens/mo given their query distribution and expected caching.
- Action item: run a 2-week Dedicated POC (reserved 2x A100-equivalent slots) to validate throughput, autoscaling behavior, and quantization profile in real traffic.

Quotes / call snippets:
- CTO: "We need predictable bill run rate — variable costs make forecasts impossible for FY27."
- Product lead: "If we can shave 25–40% off cost with no UX regressions, Dedicated is worth the ops lift."

Open items / Blockers:
- Procurement needs formal SOW + pricing tier for Dedicated; finance asking for committed discount schedule.
- Security team needs KMS integration diagram and third-party SOC2 evidence (AE provided link to Redwood security FAQ).
- SE needs approval to run long-form quantization tests on production-like prompts — request from product for narrow-intent regression set.
